items.title: Travelodge’s New CEO Inherits Safety Reckoning, Rising Costs and Looming Debt
items.summary: Travelodge has a new chief executive, 38 safety recommendations to implement, and debt to refinance. Peter Krueger starts Tuesday.

items.title: Norse Atlantic Suspends Flights as Bankruptcy Looms
items.summary: Norse’s cash crisis extends far beyond its own operations, forcing international airline and cruise partners to reassess their flying plans.

items.title: Heathrow’s Third Runway Has a $25 Billion Problem Before It Gets to Emissions
items.summary: The fight over Heathrow's third runway has been about whether it fits net zero. Lawmakers have now added a more basic question: who pays, and how much ends up in fares? Until ministers can answer that, and price in the cost of cutting emissions, the plan is stalled.

items.title: Houthi Attacks Gut Riyadh’s Peak Season
items.summary: Riyadh’s fourth quarter runs on international corporate and event demand that flies in, and the missile strikes hit that badly. Domestic demand can’t fill the gap, so hotels will trade rate for occupancy in the quarter that in normal times supports their strongest pricing.

items.title: Middle East Tourism Has Split. Which Demand Gets Capital?
items.summary: Gulf travel now runs at two speeds. Pilgrimage and resort demand held through 2026, while long-haul and corporate travel fell away. Every 2027 capital and capacity plan for the region depends on which market an operator underwrites.

items.title: Clarins Family Takes Full Ownership of Luxury Hotel Group Evok
items.summary: The Courtin family behind the Clarins skincare empire  is combining what the hotel industry usually splits apart: the buildings, the brands, and the operations of a luxury hotel group, under one owner.
